correctness.rationale: The coarea-normalized convolution identity is exact. Integer beta exponents give finitely many polynomial branches and joint algebraicity. One half-integral exponent gives an arcsin term with explicit nonzero polynomial coefficient; two half-integral exponents give a nonzero internal-knot logarithm. Equal radii with odd first log order are treated by one additional analytic expansion, producing a nonzero even-order log coefficient. Symbolic checker replayed the (3,3) polynomial and exact (2,2),(2,4),(4,4) log coefficients, with numerical integration as supplementary evidence. Axial and endpoint cases are bounded as stated.

originality.rationale: An explicit hypothesis-and-implication comparison was made against Fish–Ryabogin–Sun–Yaskin (arXiv:2610.10229v1, Sections 1/4), Agranovsky (arXiv:2409.19373v1), the Agranovsky et al. survey (arXiv:2212.07510), and classical smooth polynomial-integrability work (arXiv:1702.00429). Published-record searches for product-ball algebraic Radon transforms, beta convolutions, equivalent cutoff-volume notions and logarithmic knots yielded no covering result. The smoothness/local finite-rank assumptions in the closest rigidity theorems do not subsume these piecewise-algebraic nonsmooth products. A classical convolution identity is acknowledged. Historical priority is not certified against all unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The complete natural two-factor family shows odd/odd exactly characterizes algebraic cutoff volume, supplying curved nonsmooth nonpolyhedral even-dimensional examples and the first obstruction in other parities. The equal-radius cancellation and surviving higher log order are structural, non-routine analytic phenomena important for Radon section regularity, not a single arbitrary numerical invariant.
